lectures.title: Reflection and the mirror formula
lectures.notes:
The mirror formula links object distance u, image distance v and focal length f: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.

For a concave mirror f is negative in the New Cartesian sign convention. Magnification m = -v/u; a negative m means the image is inverted.

lectures.title: Refraction and Snell's law
lectures.notes:
When light passes from one medium to another it bends. Snell's law: n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r).

Light bends towards the normal when it enters a denser medium (higher n).

questions.q: Light enters glass from air. It bends…
questions.explanation: Entering a denser medium slows light, so it bends towards the normal.

questions.q: A magnification of -2 means the image is…
questions.explanation: Negative m = inverted; |m| = 2 = twice the size.

questions.q: Which law relates the angles of incidence and refraction?
questions.hint: n1 sin i = n2 sin r.
questions.explanation: Snell's law describes refraction at a boundary.

faq.q: Why does a straw look bent in water?
faq.a: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves water into air, so your eye traces it back along a different line, making the straw look bent.
